questions.stem: A nitrogen atom has 5 electrons in its outer shell. How many covalent bonds does it typically form?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen has 5 outer electrons and needs 3 more to complete its outer shell of 8. It forms 3 covalent bonds by sharing 3 of its electrons with other atoms. For example, in ammonia (NH₃), nitrogen shares one electron with each of 3 hydrogen atoms, forming 3 single covalent bonds.

options.text: The transfer of electrons from one atom to another
A shared pair of electrons between two atoms
The attraction between positive and negative ions
A delocalised sea of electrons around metal ions

questions.explanation: A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between two atoms. Each atom contributes one electron to the shared pair (in a standard bond). The shared electrons are attracted to both nuclei, holding the atoms together. This type of bonding typically occurs between non-metal atoms.

questions.stem: Oxygen forms a double bond in O₂. What does this mean in terms of electrons?

options.text: Two shared pairs of electrons (4 electrons total) are involved in the bond
One shared pair of electrons is twice as strong

questions.explanation: A double bond consists of two shared pairs of electrons, meaning 4 electrons are involved in the bonding. Each oxygen atom contributes 2 electrons to the double bond. Oxygen has 6 outer electrons and needs 2 more for a full shell, so it forms 2 bonds (a double bond). Double bonds are shorter and stronger than single bonds.

questions.stem: Water (H₂O) has two bonding pairs and two lone pairs on the oxygen atom. How does this affect the molecule's shape?

options.text: The molecule is linear because there are only 2 bonds
The lone pairs repel the bonding pairs, making the molecule bent/V-shaped
The lone pairs have no effect on shape
The molecule is square because there are 4 electron pairs

questions.explanation: Lone pairs of electrons repel bonding pairs more strongly than bonding pairs repel each other. In water, the two lone pairs on oxygen push the two bonding pairs closer together, creating a bent or V-shaped molecule with a bond angle of about 104.5° instead of 180°.

questions.stem: Carbon has 4 outer electrons. What is the molecular formula of the simplest compound carbon forms with hydrogen?
questions.explanation: Carbon needs 4 more electrons to fill its outer shell, so it forms 4 covalent bonds. Each hydrogen atom has 1 outer electron and needs 1 more, forming 1 bond. Therefore carbon bonds with 4 hydrogen atoms, giving CH₄ (methane). Each C-H bond is a single covalent bond with one shared pair of electrons.
